lines.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, good morning to you!
Hey, Viktor, I am not giving you money!
I already paid you two paychecks.
What did you want?
Why, I am not calling for money!
Really? Then why are you calling?
Tonight is an important football match.
Is your beloved Spartak playing again?
Yes, and I have reliable insider info!
Viktor, sports betting is dangerous.
I need a small advance until tomorrow.
I know your advances, Viktor.
You will not get a single kopeck!
Dmitry, you will regret this!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: money paid before the work is done

examples.text: Степан Геннадьевич, я же внёс аванс!
examples.trans: Stepan Gennadyevich, I did pay the advance!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

examples.text: А я вообще очень верная женщина.
examples.trans: And I am actually a very loyal woman.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выдать.gloss: to issue, give out, hand out

examples.trans: The cashier issued the money against the receipt.

examples.text: Ну что, судьба тебе сдачу выдала!
examples.trans: Well then, fate gave you change back!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: жить на зарплату = to live on one's salary

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
We need information on all the residents.

examples.text: В этой квартире нам нужны уши. Нужна информация по всем жильцам.
examples.trans: In that flat we need ears. We need information on all the residents.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.en: kopeck, one hundredth of a rouble
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'kopeck' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'match, game' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тихо, Сеня! Сейчас идёт решающий матч!
examples.trans: Quiet, Senya! A decisive match is on right now!

examples.text: Кто сегодня играет на этом матче?
examples.trans: Who is playing in this match today?

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'большой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, modest').

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.

examples.text: Мы живём в небольшом тихом городе.
examples.trans: We live in a small, quiet town.

examples.text: Извините, у нас тут небольшой бардак.
examples.trans: Excuse us, we have a bit of a mess here.

meanings.note: + genitive: ни копейки = not a penny

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dangerous').

examples.trans: This is a very dangerous job.

examples.text: У меня много опасных друзей. А иначе я позвоню ребятам.
examples.trans: I have many dangerous friends. Otherwise I'll call the guys.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: ты ещё пожалеешь! = you'll be sorry!

examples.text: Ты знаешь, сколько у меня денег? Ты ещё пожалеешь!
examples.trans: Do you know how much money I have? You'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне придётся = I'll have to

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sport, sports' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там наливают бесплатно, если сделать ставку.
examples.trans: They pour for free if you place a bet.
The bets are placed, no more bets.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
An important football match is starting.
Tonight is an important football match.

examples.text: У Виктора сейчас начинается важный футбольный матч.
examples.trans: Viktor has an important football match starting now.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
